Mark the student's response to a question from the 2015 NSW HSC Business Studies exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 23(c) [2 marks]: Recommend a method of monitoring the effectiveness of the process layout.
STIMULUS / CASE INFORMATION:
North Coast Manufacturing makes customised furniture for its clients.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 2):
2 marks: Provides a method of monitoring with a reason in favour of that method
1 marks: Makes a relevant statement

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
One method of monitoring the effectiveness of the new layout would be to compare the output of the old layout over a given time period, with the output of the new layout, over a similar time period. This would clearly provide managers with comparative information regarding the volume of products produced in a given period.

ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
• better quality of output
• waste minimisation
• shorter lead times
• greater productivity



STUDENT RESPONSE:

Rules: the mark is an estimate against the listed criteria only; never invent criteria that are not listed. Quote the student's own words as evidence for every mark you award. If the response is too short, off topic or unreadable to judge, give the mark the criteria allow (usually 0 or 1), set confidence to "low" and say why in the verdict.

Return JSON only, no prose, in this exact shape:
{"mark": <integer 0-2>, "band": "<the criteria row it fits, e.g. '2'>", "verdict": "<one sentence saying why it got that mark>", "evidence": ["<up to 3 short quotes, under 15 words each, taken word for word from the student's response, that earned marks; [] if none>"], "strengths": ["<up to 3 short points>"], "missing": ["<up to 3 elements the criteria row above this one needs and the response lacks>"], "improvements": ["<up to 3 concrete things to add or change to reach the next row, each under 25 words>"], "next": "<the single most useful next action for this student, under 20 words>", "confidence": "<high, medium or low>", "model": "<a full-mark answer in 2 to 5 plain sentences a student could realistically write in the exam>"}
